note: The Mac: the same values of the hand as linux.json (path, press, keys: part B, board ab-t30.13; the research, docs/research/2026-11-09-click-box-input-signals.md, section 8.3), with timestamps that keep their fraction (C11). The other values of the device (whole px, the wheel) stay Linux's after board ab-t30.32 (step B of the input fit, with the Mac probe on Chrome 158, macOS arm64): whole px, because no probe has shown yet that a fraction of a CDP point reaches a page on the Mac (step B1 does not pass, and step B2, the moves of less than 1 px, does not start); and the notches of 120 px, because a CDP mouseWheel on the Mac gives wheelDeltaY -120 for a deltaY of 13 and of 120 (step B3); each value names its source in sources.

sources.device.rateMs: 125 Hz, the rate of the research's X input (C11 STAGE_MOVE_MS = 8); [7]: mice report typically at 100 Hz; part B: the person's sample gaps have a median of 8.1 ms (p10 7.9, p90 8.3), and 8.0 ms is inside them (the research, docs/research/2026-11-09-click-box-input-signals.md, section 8.3, point 1; board ab-t30.13 keeps 8 ms)
sources.device.latencyMs: C11 STAGE_LATENCY_MS (3 to 5 ms); the design's probe M1: 4 ms before the send gave a frame phase of 5.4 to 5.6 ms
sources.device.maxPxPerMs: 8 px/ms between two samples (C11 maxSpeedPxPerMs; board ab-t30.13): part B's peak speed of a move has a median of 3.56 px/ms, a p90 of 7.73 and a maximum of 13.38, and 11 of 20 moves are above the first value of 3.5 ([13]) (the research, docs/research/2026-11-09-click-box-input-signals.md, section 8.3, point 4); at 8 ms a step is then at most 64 px, below the harness's jump of 100 px (R1, R2)
sources.path.fitts: Fitts's law, a = 250 ms, b = 110 ms a bit, 300 to 1000 ms (src/record.ts fittsMs); a lognormal spread of sigma 0.2 [18]
sources.path.arc: one main sub-movement with a bell speed (minimum jerk) along an arc to one side [17], 2% to 16% of the distance: fitted (board ab-t30.13) to part B's straightness, a median of 0.95 with 10 of 20 moves above 0.94 (the research, docs/research/2026-11-09-click-box-input-signals.md, section 8.3, point 4; the first values of 2% to 10% put 85% of the moves above 0.94, PR #109); the generator's moves of task 2's kind: about half above 0.94
sources.path.corrections: the approach (board ab-t30.13): the main sub-movement takes the first 18% of the time and ends 7% to 15% of the distance short of the target (at most 1.5 times its width plus 4 px, and 1% of the distance to one side); 1 or 2 corrective sub-movements (in 95% of moves; 45% one, 50% two) then bring the pointer slowly to the target in the last 82% of the time ([14] models sub-movements). When the speed limit stretches the main sub-movement past Fitts's longest time (C11's 1000 ms), the approach gives that time back, down to a floor of approachMinShare (40%) of its own time and approachMsPerPx (0.5 ms) for each px of the main's end error, so a path keeps C11's 1000 ms while 8 px/ms allows it (review-217 B1: in a 1280 x 900 viewport every path with no overshoot; a path with no overshoot goes past 1000 ms only from about 2900 px). Fitted to part B: the peak speed of task 2's moves (a median of 3.56 px/ms, 11 of 20 above 3.5; the generator: about 3.9 and about 57%), and the click box's approach, 25 to 65 samples inside its 300 x 65 frame before the press (a median of 41, a p90 of 47) in 236 to 747 ms from the entry to the press (a median of 518) (the research, docs/research/2026-11-09-click-box-input-signals.md, section 8.3, points 4 and 5; the generator: a median of about 41 samples, and about 510 ms from the entry to the last sample)
sources.path.overshoot: for a move of more than 500 px, 2% to 8% past the target in about 30% of moves, then the way back (first values)
sources.path.jitter: 0.3 to 1.2 px across the path at 8 to 12 Hz, a hand's tremor (first value, no source)
sources.path.approach: the main sub-movement's time warp (below 1: an earlier peak and a slower end of its bell): 0.62 to 0.75 for a small target (40 px or less), 0.8 to 0.95 for a larger one (the research, P4), for a path with no corrections and for an overshoot; the approach of path.corrections (board ab-t30.13) gives the slow end, and its fast main sub-movement keeps mainWarpShare (0.3) of the warp's distance from 1 (a warp of 0.89 to 0.99), so its first step stays short: with the whole warp 74% of those moves made a first step over 4 px on an axis, with 0.3 of it about 2%; and the stage cuts a drag's first step to 4 px on each axis (src/relay/stage.ts DRAG_FIRST_STEP_PX, review-217 N1), so a drag always starts at a later move (C11, the drag: a person's path starts with short moves)
sources.path.start: the page's last point; with none, a random point of the viewport's middle 30% to 70%
sources.path.short: a short move, a step of mouse.move with steps (C11, the pointer: "`mouseMoved` with no button down, at most 50 px from the page's last point: samples of the client's line at the rate of the device." and "Their speed is 0.5 to 1.5 px/ms, with 0 to 1 px of jitter across the line."; design 5.1, the steps row)
sources.press.pauseMs: a lognormal, median 49.5 ms, sigma 0.31, from 25 to 190 ms (C11 pauseMs), counted from the last sample that moves the pointer 1 px or more (board ab-t30.13): part B's last sample 1 px or more from the press point comes a median of 49.5 ms before the press (p10 35.3, p90 78.2; 26.1 to 188.9); sigma ln(78.2 / 35.3) / (2 x 1.2816) = 0.31 (the research, docs/research/2026-11-09-click-box-input-signals.md, section 8.3, point 6; the time from the last pointermove, a median of 19.1 ms, holds the trackpad's moves of less than 1 px, which a path in whole px does not send)
sources.press.holdMs: a lognormal, median 87.6 ms, sigma 0.20, from 60 to 180 ms (C11 holdMs): part B's 38 presses of the steps (70.8 to 154.3 ms) fit a lognormal with a median of 87.6 and a sigma of 0.20 (the research, docs/research/2026-11-09-click-box-input-signals.md, section 8.3, point 6); force 0.5 [1]
sources.press.doubleGapMs: 90 to 150 ms from the first release to the second press (not measured; part B)
sources.press.spread: an offset from the target's middle, a normal with a standard deviation of 1/8 of its smaller side, at most 1/4 of it
sources.press.modifierAfterMs: the release of a click's modifier key, Playwright's ensureModifiers (C11, the pointer: "The stage holds the modifier's `keyUp` until 60 to 200 ms after the mouse release"; design 5.1, the modifiers row)
sources.device.wholePx: true: the samples of a path and of a short move in whole CSS px, on the Mac too, and the points that the stage chooses itself (a wheel point of the grid, the spread point, the point of its own click); a press and its release at the client's point, and the notches at the page's last point when that point is the client's, keep the client's fraction on the Mac, and a step that starts at a client's point keeps that point's fraction there (the drag's short first step from a press at the client's point; the hold's press and its 1 px hand steps when the hold's hover sends no path) (C11, the timestamps and the rate; board ab-t30.32, step B1, which does not pass). A person's pointer events on the Mac all have a fraction (part B: 3208 of 3208 pointermove, 64 of 64 pointerdown and 63 of 63 pointerup events; the research, docs/research/2026-11-09-click-box-input-signals.md, sections 3 and 8.3, point 10), but no probe has shown yet that a fraction of a CDP point reaches a page on the Mac: the Mac probe (test/live/mac-input-probe/, commit 7988db0; Chrome 158.0.8127.37 on macOS arm64, 2026-11-24) moved the pointer to 300.37, 200.61 through the stage's whole-px path, and the page got clientX 300 and clientY 201, with a fraction in 0 of 59 pointermove events. So the moves of less than 1 px of step B2 do not start either
sources.wheel: a notch of 120 px (X11); gaps of 35 to 90 ms (design 8.2, first value). The Mac gets the same notches (board ab-t30.32, step B3): the Mac probe (test/live/mac-input-probe/, commit 7988db0; Chrome 158.0.8127.37 on macOS arm64, 2026-11-24) sent a CDP mouseWheel of deltaY 13 and one of deltaY 120, and each gave one wheel event with wheelDeltaY -120 (deltaMode 0), as on Linux; so a train of small deltas, as part B's trackpad gives (a median |deltaY| of 13 px, wheelDeltaY about -3 x deltaY; the research, section 8.3, point 8), would show -120 on each event, which a trackpad does not give
sources.population: each scope's person: factors drawn once from these spreads (design 10.4; first values: part B recorded one person, so it sets the centre, the values of the hand above, and not the spread of the population)
sources.population.keySpeed: a factor on the time from one key press to the next, drawn once for the scope (design 10.2 and 10.4: an average typist's mean is 239 ms, a fast one's about 120 ms [19]); the spread of the pointer's speed
sources.keys.holdMs: a lognormal per key, median 80.3 ms, sigma 0.23, from 50 to 250 ms (C11 keyHoldMs): part B's holds have a median of 80.3 ms, a mean of 81.8 and an SD of 19.0, so sigma sqrt(ln(1 + (19.0 / 81.8)^2)) = 0.23 (the research, docs/research/2026-11-09-click-box-input-signals.md, section 8.3, point 9); the floor of 50 ms cuts about 2% of the draws (5 of the person's 106 holds are below it; the first value: mean 116 ms, SD 24 ms [19])
sources.keys.baseMs: the base part of the time from one press to the next (design 10.2), times the person's key speed and the drift: a lognormal, median 100 ms, sigma 0.3, from 40 to 1500 ms, fitted (board ab-t30.13; test/human-keys.test.ts) with keys.pairMs and keys.pauseMs on part B's three task lines (recorder.html, task 3) to part B's press to press, a median of 128.9 ms and a mean of 207 ms, and its overlap share of 16.5% (17 of 103 keys) (the research, docs/research/2026-11-09-click-box-input-signals.md, section 8.3, point 9): the middle person gives a median of about 129 ms, a mean of about 207 ms and a share of about 16%; at that mean about 48 characters fit in 10 s (C11, the typing rule: about 40 to 50). The mean holds part B's 4 corrections (Backspace), which the plan has none of (K5); the first fit: lognormal 125 ms, sigma 0.75, for 25% of rollover [19]
sources.keys.pairMs: the letter pair's part (ms, times the key speed and the drift; never below 0, so a release that is not answered early is never passed by the next press): two hands (or the space's thumb) 0, one hand 30, one finger 50, one key twice 30; the fit of keys.baseMs (part B gives no pair with enough values of its own)
sources.keys.pauseMs: more time after a space (80 to 480 ms) and after a mark .,;:!? (320 to 1000 ms): the fit of keys.baseMs, which gives part B's long tail of the press to press (a mean of 207 ms against a median of 128.9; the first values: 20 to 120 and 80 to 250 ms); after Enter, a line's end, 200 to 600 ms (design 10.2, a first value: part B typed each line as a step of its own) (the research's K2: longer at word and line ends [19], [20])
sources.keys.drift: the speed in a session: a factor from 0.85 to 1.15 that drifts from word to word, a random walk of its log that keeps 0.8 of its last value with a normal step of SD 0.05 (design 10.2, first value)
sources.keys.shift: a Shift rawKeyDown a lognormal of median 147.7 ms and sigma 0.59 before a shifted character, from 45 to 480 ms (C11 shiftBeforeMs; part B: a median of 147.7 ms, 47.8 to 471.8, 10 shifted characters; sigma ln(480 / 45) / 4); its release 15 to 60 ms after the release of the last key that it holds (C11 shiftAfterMs; part B: a median of 38.0 ms); the Shift of the other hand's side in about 70% of cases (C11, the keys: "In about 70% of cases"; part B: 5 of the 8 Shift presses with a side, shiftOtherHand of shiftSided, which is inside the spread of 8 draws at 70%; a fit of 0.625 needs a change of that C11 sentence, which is not in board ab-t30.13's step A) (the research, docs/research/2026-11-09-click-box-input-signals.md, section 8.3, point 9; the first values: 45 to 95 ms, and 70%)
sources.keys.chord: in a chord, each modifier 40 to 120 ms before the key, the releases 20 to 80 ms apart in reverse order (C11 chordBeforeMs, chordReleaseGapMs)
sources.keys.afterReleaseMs: a key that waits for a release (the same key again, a key after the release of Shift or of a chord's modifier) goes 5 to 30 ms after it (first value)
sources.keys.fastMs: the fast end of the person's spread, 100 to 120 ms a key, with no pair part and no pause (C11 fastKeyMs; design 7.2)
sources.keys.runSlowMs: a key run at the person's speed for 12 s, then at the fast end (C11 STAGE_RUN_SLOW_MS; the answer Q2 a); keys.typeMaxMs: the typing rule's 10 s (C11 STAGE_TYPE_MAX_MS)
